title: SQL injection in /item id parameter

proof.requirement: the DBMS fingerprint plus at least one row from a named table, bounded to what proves the read

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes
rows returned, not an error message

description: id is interpolated into the query string. The quote probe returns a raw sqlite error; a UNION SELECT limited to five rows returns credentials from the users table.

title: OS command injection in /ping host parameter

proof.requirement: the output of `id; echo <nonce>` returned by the target, with the nonce tying the output to the probe

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes
identity output returned by the target
the probe nonce came back in the output

description: host is concatenated into a shell command. `id; echo <nonce>` returns the server's own identity line and the nonce, so the output is computed by the target and not reflected.
remediation: Never pass request data to a shell; exec with an argv list and validate the host as an address.

title: Reflected XSS in /search q parameter

proof.requirement: a headless browser executing the payload and reporting the probe nonce

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes

checks.detail: this system has no browser, so execution is not provable here. Drive one over mcp_call and cite the nonce it reports, or leave this a candidate and say so in the report

description: Canary chars < > " ' reflect unescaped in an html context. Execution is not shown here - this engagement had no browser, so the class stays a candidate.

title: IDOR: /api/user/<id> serves any user object

proof.requirement: one actor reaching another's subject on the same endpoint, with subject-identifying data and nothing entitling the caller to it

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes
two distinct object references on one endpoint

checks.detail: present in r22, absent from r20

checks.check: the caller was not entitled to it
checks.detail: no credential was presented and subject data came back

description: Object ids are not checked against the caller. Reading id 2 returns alice; reading id 1 returns the admin record, with no credential distinguishing the two requests.

title: Exposed /.env and /.git/HEAD at web root

proof.requirement: the credential or source observed in a response, quoted as the bytes that leaked

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes
it came from a response, not from the request

description: Sensitive paths are served publicly - credentials and source-control metadata leak to anyone.
remediation: Deny dotfile/VCS paths at the web server; rotate exposed secrets.

title: JWT weak secret: forged admin token accepted

proof.requirement: a credential this system minted, accepted on a privileged resource with its claims echoed back, and another credential refused on the same endpoint

checks.check: the target produced the quoted bytes
the same endpoint refuses another credential

description: The session JWT verifies against the dictionary secret 'secret123'. A token forged offline with role=admin is accepted and its claims echoed back; the same request with a broken signature is refused with 401, so the endpoint does verify - against a guessable key.
remediation: Rotate to a high-entropy secret; prefer asymmetric signing.
